summary: Both files are core formal mathematics content in the ArkLib coding theory library. LinearCode.lean (839 lines) defines linear codes, weight/projection lemmas, singleton bounds, MDS codes, generator matrices, dimension/rate, and distance/weight theorems with proofs. MDSGenerator.lean (553 lines) formalizes mutual correlated agreement for MDS generators per BCGM25, including the MCA error function, codeword span lemmas, Hamming distance bounds, maximal agreement/CA domain lemmas (6.4–6.6), and the main theorem (6.1). Both contain definitions, theorems, and proofs with citations to coding theory literature. Neither is a pure import aggregator, test fixture, or QA tool.

summary: All 12 files contain formal mathematical content relevant to search. ArkLib.lean is a pure import aggregator (only `public import` statements), but per FILTER-007 such files should be tagged/ranked as `navigation-import-only` rather than hard-excluded. The other 11 files define core interaction/oracle execution machinery, prefix structures, witness-indexed knowledge extraction (RoundExtractor, KnowledgeCertificate), round-by-round soundness (OrdinaryState, ChallengeModel, FreshVerifier), local-to-global soundness theorems, and native Sumcheck round-by-round soundness. The three test files are compile-time acceptance examples verifying the main theorems with concrete instances (dependent knowledge composition, native failure scope, full Sumcheck invocation) — they are not QA tools or synthetic fixtures.
